title: "Pets and Babies: Comparing Popular Names"

## Project Description

This project explores the popularity of cat and dog names in Seattle and compares them with popular baby names in the United States. We aim to identify similarities and differences in naming patterns across pets and babies, including whether certain names are popular in both groups. By analyzing and visualizing naming data, we hope to better understand how naming preferences vary between pets and humans.

## Research Questions

1. What are the similarities and differences between the most popular cat and dog names in Seattle and baby names in the United States?

2. To what extent do naming preferences differ between cats and dogs, and how do these patterns compare with those of human babies?

3. How have popular pet and baby names changed over time, and are there any common trends in naming preferences?

## Motivation

We chose this topic because we are interested in how people choose names for their pets and children. Many pets have traditionally human names, which made us curious about whether popular cat and dog names overlap with popular baby names. We also wanted to explore whether naming preferences differ between cats and dogs.

By comparing these naming patterns, we hope to better understand the similarities and differences in how people name their pets and children. This topic also provides an opportunity to work with real-world datasets and explore interesting patterns through data visualization.

## Potential Datasets

We plan to use two publicly available datasets for our project.

### 1. Seattle Pets Dataset

This dataset contains 52,519 pet registration records from Seattle between 2003 and 2018, including pet names, species, breeds, and license issue dates.

We will use this dataset to identify the most popular cat and dog names and compare naming preferences between the two species.

**Source:** [OpenIntro Seattle Pets Dataset](https://www.openintro.org/data/index.php?data=seattlepets)

### 2. U.S. Baby Names Dataset

This dataset, provided by the Social Security Administration (SSA), includes baby names, birth years, sex, and the number of births associated with each name.

We will use this dataset to identify popular baby names and compare them with pet names.

**Source:** [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/limits.html)

By combining these datasets, we hope to explore similarities and differences in naming preferences among cats, dogs, and babies. We also plan to use data visualization to identify popular names and examine naming trends over time.
